name: WebAuthn PRF and largeBlob extensions
plain: Derives a secret from a passkey or stores a small blob on it.
meaning: Lets an app use the passkey as a key for end to end encryption (PRF is a 32 byte HMAC output). largeBlob stores small data on the authenticator.

access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

data.metric: Derives a secret from a passkey or stores a small blob on it.

fields.name: largeBlob.blob
fields.range: typically up to about 1 KB on current authenticators

limits.headline: Can use your passkey to make an encryption key or store a tiny note on it
limits.user_action: You tap Unlock or Sign in on an app that protects your data with a passkey
can: Ask your passkey to make a secret value, 32 bytes long, for locking your data
Lock and unlock your data on your device with that secret
Store a small piece of data on a security key that supports it
cannot: Make the secret without your passkey confirmation
Store large files on the passkey

story.what_it_is: Lets a site use your passkey as the key to lock and unlock your private data.

marketing.name: WebAuthn extensions (PRF)
marketing.pitch: Documents an extension that lets a site derive secret keys from a passkey for tasks like end to end encryption.

story.for_you: You may notice a notes or vault app that unlocks with your face or fingerprint and no extra password. The same tap that signs you in also opens your encrypted data.
story.for_makers: Makers of private apps can offer end to end encryption without asking for a separate master password. It improves security and convenience, and it lets them say even they cannot read user data.

use_cases.example: A password manager web vault unlocks with a passkey, so there is no master password to forget.
A secure notes or chat web app derives its encryption key from the passkey, so messages stay unreadable on its servers.
A health records web app encrypts files with a passkey derived key so a data leak exposes nothing readable.
A cloud drafts tool encrypts unpublished writing and designs with a key that only the person's device can unlock.
A browser game launcher could encrypt saved credentials and payment tokens with the passkey, so a stolen database is useless.
A security team uses it to protect secrets in the browser without storing a key in a cookie.

risks: Lose the passkey, lose the data

technical_bounds: Support varies by authenticator and OS
Firefox PRF partial (macOS and Windows 139+, not Android)
Safari status unclear; largeBlob support not verified

abuse: Misuse is limited by origin binding

history.change: Windows Hello hmac-secret support (KB5077181) enables PRF on Windows
